title: ts_headline() StartSel longer than PG_INT16_MAX overflows an int16 length, ~32 KB -- leaves its block
live_proof: upstream 3ed3dbbf44, "Fix overflows with ts_headline()" (CVE-2026-6473), backpatched through 14 and therefore absent at the 17.5 pin. Upstream: the StartSel, StopSel and FragmentDelimiter options of ts_headline() have their lengths stored as int16, so a value longer than PG_INT16_MAX overflows the stored length and generateHeadline() then writes with it. The trigger here is repeat('x', 32768), which is PG_INT16_MAX + 1 exactly. Independently established on the pin by host ASan, which reports negative-size-param -- the negative size being the overflowed int16 -- and by the purecap arm, where the ~32 KB overflow leaves its block and raises SIGPROT on both the plain and the cassert build.
fidelity: real server, real allocator. Unlike case 01 this one leaves its block, which is why both a sanitizer and a capability machine can see it

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: SIGPROT on the plain purecap build -- CHERI-DETECTED (2026-10-04). SIGPROT(34) on BOTH the plain and the cassert purecap build. ~32 KB overflow leaves the malloc block, so the capability bound is crossed.
cheribsd-revocation.run: run 2026-10-06 by the corpus's own runner (shared/run-arm.py for the Capstone arms, shared/run-cheribsd.sh for the purecap one); see results/

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, PostgreSQL's contexts stock (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng): a fault after the trigger started that its control.sql or a justified fault_sites ties to the defect, or the trigger completes and this arm did not see it

status: measured on virtual Capstone (virtual-malloc, virtual-pg-pools) and stock CheriBSD (cheribsd-revocation); each arm's verdict_from names its bundle. The physical spatial/sublet pair measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-10 stays in results/
nested_why: The object is a palloc chunk, which AllocSet carves out of a block it took from malloc, so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
